commits.author: trevor@twentyideas.com <trevor@twentyideas.com>
commits.subject: Lead status with the review deck and add check --covers review
commits.body:
status now answers first with how completely the change's review deck
explains it. A new "review" coverage area measures each open review whose
head is the comparison's head over its own range (every open review when
observing); a change with no review is uncovered and asks for one.

A Saga that holds only reviews is reported review first: its documentation
areas, the implementation deck's changed-source actions, and growth
suggestions shrink to one quiet line, a short offer once it holds more than
two reviews, and the full report with --growth (always in --json, with a
growth object). A Saga with living documentation keeps the full report.

check --covers review asks whether the review deck explains every changed
line. An unknown cover target's hint now lists open reviews' slides and Items.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: trevor@twentyideas.com <trevor@twentyideas.com>
commits.subject: Let query children navigate reviews
commits.body:
query children lists each review beneath the Saga's root, and its deck,
slides, and Items beneath it, so an agent that reads Saga state only
through query can find a review's slides and Items. Review Items' code is
not indexed as documentation diff selectors.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: trevor@twentyideas.com <trevor@twentyideas.com>
commits.subject: Let review create work out its id and base
commits.body:
review create no longer needs --id or --base. When gh is installed and
origin is on GitHub it reads the branch's pull request (number, URL,
title, base); otherwise --base defaults to origin's default branch (or a
local main/master) and --id to pr-N for --pr, else the branch name. It
says what it worked out. Explicit flags still win, and CHANGE_SAGA_NO_GH=1
skips gh.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: trevor@twentyideas.com <trevor@twentyideas.com>
commits.subject: Lead init and help with a review; set up the full Saga after a few
commits.body:
init's next steps now start with a review of the branch or pull request
(review create, add-slide, set-slide-content, add-item, cover
--changed-lines, review list, check --covers review), say that sagafying a
PR is the best way to learn the tool, and put personas, stories, and
features after a few reviews. Documenting existing code stays second.

Top-level help leads with the review story and flow; implementation decks,
reconcile, and living documentation move to "Growing the Saga".

setup-initial-saga is positioned as the step after a few reviews: it grows
a Saga that holds only reviews without --overhaul, reads its reviews as
evidence, and with no Saga suggests a review first. Help with no Saga does
too.

commits.body:

this PR": review create, one slide per architectural idea, items, cover
--changed-lines, and confirmation with review list and check --covers
review. One light offer to grow the Saga follows, only after the review.
Reconciling living documentation after a review now happens only when the
Saga holds living documentation or the user asks. ci.md documents the
review area.

commits.body:

The full model follows as growing the Saga. The manual workflow, the

commits.subject: Never pitch growing the Saga; just make the path clear
commits.body:
A team may never adopt the Saga as documentation, and that is fine. status
no longer counts reviews or offers growth: a Saga that holds only reviews
gets the review-first report and nothing else, and --full (renamed from
--growth) shows every area when asked. The JSON's .growth becomes
.documentation {living_documentation, report}. The skill drops its growth
offer. init, help, setup-initial-saga, the README, and the docs say a Saga
of reviews alone is complete and explain how to grow it if the team wants.

commits.author: trevor@twentyideas.com <trevor@twentyideas.com>
commits.subject: Measure the review over the change and match it by the branch it follows
commits.body:
Fixes from the independent review of PR #9:

1. A stacked pull request's review reported the whole change complete. The
   review area is now measured over the comparison's own changed lines
   against the matched reviews' Items, and names the narrower range when a
   review's base differs.
2. A review that followed HEAD claimed the next branch's change after its
   own landed. review create records the checked-out branch as --head;
   matching skips merged reviews, and a review that follows HEAD once its
   evidence shows an earlier change. review follow pins an existing review.
3. A review whose range could not be resolved read as "no review". Reviews
   are matched by their followed head (origin/<branch> too), on a detached
   CI head or GitHub's merge commit; bases fall back to origin/<base>; the
   defaults prefer origin/<branch>.
4. review create --head asked gh about the checked-out branch; it now asks
   about the head, and bounds gh with WaitDelay.

Also: a "create a review" next action for any unreviewed comparison, a
companion Saga's sync.json counts as review-only, printed commands keep
--repo, review create --json reports what it inferred, and the README gains
an opt-in "Use it in CI" section. This repository's CI now runs check
--covers review on its own pull requests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: trevor@twentyideas.com <trevor@twentyideas.com>
commits.subject: Match fork pull requests and pin rewritten reviews instead of duplicating
commits.body:
From the re-review of c1306536:

1. A fork's branch never exists in the base repository's CI clone, so its
   review was never matched. A review whose branch does not resolve now
   matches when its evidence is part of this change; one whose evidence
   landed still never does.
2. The README's CI example pinned a v0.2.0 that does not exist. It now
   uses a marked CHANGE_SAGA_VERSION placeholder for both the URL and
   --version, with a note to use v0.2.0-rc.6 or later.
3. A review that follows HEAD whose evidence was rewritten by an amend,
   rebase, or squash gets a review follow suggestion instead of review
   create; evidence pinned at the comparison's base (deleted lines only)
   counts as this change's.

commits.author: trevor@twentyideas.com <trevor@twentyideas.com>
commits.subject: Keep a replaced coverage record with its owner by default
commits.body:
replace-coverage without --target resolved the replacement against the
default target, the Saga root, so the evidence silently left its Item.
reconcile's printed repair path names no target, so following it did
exactly that. A replacement now stays with the record's owner unless
--target (or a batch record's target) says otherwise.
